statements.t: We are initially focused on our flagship project, Texas Critical Data Centers LLC (“TCDC”), a 493-acre campus in Ector County, Texas, designed to support over 1 gigawatt (“GW”) of potential compute capacity through phased development, with projected power delivery beginning as early as the end of 2027.

We believe our proximity to major natural gas pipelines, fiber networks and CO2 pipelines will provide us with the ability to serve our customers lower transmission costs and best-in-class uptime for purposes of reliably generating AI compute to capitalize on the AI revolution.

We intend to execute through partnering across engineering, construction, procurement, power generation and sustainability to provide our hyperscaler tenants with certainty of execution and speed-to-power.

In September 2026, PowerCo entered into the PPA with Luminant for 200 to 207 megawatts of firm electric energy in each hour, to be delivered to the Company’s Texas Critical Data Center project (the “Data Center Project”) from Luminant’s Odessa, Texas generating facility or other sources.

The DFA also requires the Company, following the Power Delivery Date, to issue to Luminant’s affiliate non-voting equity interests representing 5% of the entity holding the portion of the Data Center Project served under the PPA.
We have set out below a discussion of the key factors that have affected our financial performance and that are expected to impact our performance going forward.
Powered land is becoming increasingly difficult for hyperscalers to access, and we believe our projects provide “speed-to-power” in a manner differentiated from our peers.

Our ability to navigate this evolving policy landscape, especially as it pertains to grid resilience and the designation of critical infrastructure, will be an important factor in our long-term scalability and strategic positioning.

The Company reviews its deferred tax assets for recoverability and establishes a valuation allowance based on projected future taxable income, applicable tax strategies and the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences.

The Company recognizes the tax benefit from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities, based upon the technical merits of the position.

If all or a portion of the unrecognized tax benefit is sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities, the tax benefit will be recognized as a reduction to the Company’s deferred tax liability and will affect the Company’s effective tax rate in the period it is recognized.
The Company realized no Texas Margin Tax in the accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements as we do not anticipate owing any Texas Margin Tax for the periods presented.
We are currently focused in the near-term on using our available liquidity for the development of our flagship data center project, TCDC.

We expect our liquidity to be supported by a diversified mix of debt and equity capital, including project financing for the buildout of our flagship project as well as tenant prepayments and advances, strategic equity investments and government grants.

Although we plan to fund near-term development activity through a combination of these methods, there can be no assurance that such capital will be available in the amounts required or on favorable terms.

If we are unable to raise capital in the amounts, timing, or terms we expect, we may be forced to delay capital expenditures, amend or terminate our purchase commitments for long-lead materials or surrender assets pledged as collateral under our financing agreements in order to preserve liquidity, which could materially extend our development timeline and delay one or more phases of our projects, preventing us…

Under the DFA entered into on September 18, 2026, we agreed to reimburse an affiliate of Luminant construction costs for substation and transmission infrastructure serving the Data Center Project, subject to execution of definitive purchase and sale agreements and up to a cap of $116.0 million.
The cap also includes amounts to acquire the associated substation under a purchase and sale agreement that we expect to execute in the fourth quarter of 2026.
We expect reimbursable costs over the next twelve months to be significantly below the cap, although we may reach the cap, depending on final scope, equipment pricing, and construction schedule.

Including the DFA reimbursement obligations, we currently expect cash requirements of approximately $50 million to $60 million over the next twelve months, which we expect to primarily fund with cash on hand, and, as necessary, with proceeds from sales under the ATM Program, under which approximately $40 million remained available as of September 30, 2026.

Upon execution of binding term sheets or definitive agreements with one or more data center tenants and the Phase 1 purchase and sales agreement, our expected expenditures will increase materially as we proceed with the development of our flagship project.

We currently estimate total capital expenditures for the first phase of our flagship project of approximately $150 million to $400 million over the next twelve months, subject to the terms and conditions agreed with our future tenants.
If the estimates of proved reserves decline, the rate at which the Company records DD&A expense will increase, reducing future net income.

The Company continually assesses both positive and negative evidence for recoverability of its deferred tax assets and based on projected future taxable income, applicable tax strategies and the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences, the Company maintained a valuation allowance of $21.7 million as of September 30, 2026.
